sentences.text: On the morning of 16 November, before sunrise, Mars and Jupiter shine side by side on the eastern horizon.
The two planets come within just one point two degrees of each other in the sky, about two and a half full-moon widths.
Of course they are not really side by side: Mars is about three hundred million kilometres from us, Jupiter nine hundred million.
Seen from above it becomes clear: Earth, Mars and Jupiter line up along the same direction in their orbits around the Sun.
A conjunction is only a trick of perspective, but it is one of the easiest sky events to watch with the naked eye.
